body: MAINLINE-013 filed. 76 sourced cores, 47 at or below 10 kg/m3; 21/21 DOIs match Crossref. Needs are rebuilt at each core's density on 007's two splits, reproducing 007 and 007b (160/160, 17/17). No measured core at or below 10 kg/m3 passes crush, crimp and wrinkling with 6061 faces on the P2 float ceiling. Wrinkling binds. The best is the hollow alumina octet nanolattice (Meza 2014) at 5.5 kg/m3: 5.84e3x short on Ec*Gc, 18x on stress, 1.66e3x at the classical 0.76. In 008b's 1-4 kg/m3 band the best (nanoporous graphene, 3 kg/m3) is 7.6e4x short; crimp 6.3x, structural crush 11.9x. Crush is first met at 5.3 kg/m3 (hierarchical alumina, 1.34, a figure read). Crimp needs Gc 2.52 MPa; the best is 1.36x short. No source measured a shear modulus below 10 kg/m3, so Gc = Ec/2, optimistic. The lightest all-three pass is a vitreous carbon micro-lattice at 190 kg/m3 (second-hand source), where the shell's buckling SF is 0.020. Honeycombs at 16-29 kg/m3 miss honeycomb wrinkling by 216x or more, and most fail dimpling. PROJECTION: an ideal stretch-dominated lattice passes wrinkling and crimp from 1.34 kg/m3 (K13D2U-grade struts), 4.82 (beryllium) and 55.9 (6061). Measured lattices reach 3-4% of ideal; 38-98% is needed at 5 kg/m3. So the gap below 8 kg/m3 is core Ec*Gc: about 9-23x in lattice efficiency plus fibre-grade struts, or faces that lower the need. 17 NFI rows. QUESTIONABLE, not a certification.
